title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 66-68): Grothendieck wants to describe, purely in terms of profinite groupoids, extensions and outer actions, the étale 'K(π,1)' parts of smooth schemes over fields K of finite type over Q. Here E_K is the groupoid-theoretic avatar of Spec K, the 'groupoïde à lacets' carrying the action of Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q). On the previous page he started from K1 = Q(T1), the function field of the 'arithmetic sphere' P^1_Q. He built the groupoid analogue of U_{0,3} and, by 'forage des trous' (drilling holes), of U_{0,3+card I}. He suggested Raynaud's rigid-analytic yoga (discs around 0, 1, ∞) as a way to do this.

This page continues the induction ('et on remonte'). One obtains either curves of type (0,ν2) (P^1 minus ν2 points) over K1 or over a finite extension of K1. Or one obtains relative curves of type (0,ν2) over a curve over Q, or over a finite extension of Q. That base curve is itself U_{0,ν1}, or a finite étale cover of such a U_{0,ν1}. Proceeding step by step ('de proche en proche') one constructs all E_K over E_Q. This reaches every K because every finitely generated field over Q is a finite extension of a purely transcendental one. It also reaches all 'elementary models': towers in which each step is either a fibration in genus-0 curves of type (0,ν) or a finite étale cover of such a fibration.

The claim ('Sauf erreur') is that such models give a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of every point of any smooth X over any such K. The next page then proposes to rebuild smooth K-schemes by gluing these pieces along open immersions. It also calls for a more geometric language centred on rigid points, and for describing whole étale topoi, not just the K(π,1) piece.

Modern reading: this is a refinement of Artin's 'bons voisinages' (SGA 4, Exp. XI). Every point of a smooth variety over a field has a basis of neighbourhoods that are elementary fibrations, i.e. iterated smooth affine curve fibrations with finite étale boundary, and these are K(π,1). The refinement is that each curve-fibration step can be taken, up to a finite étale cover, to be a genus-0 fibration of type (0,ν). It is used to generate all of E_K and its arithmetic fundamental groups from the P^1 minus points tower and finite étale covers. This is the 'Lego/Teichmüller tower' philosophy transported to arbitrary smooth varieties.
errors: The genus-0 refinement is stated with 'sauf erreur' and no proof. It is plausible: locally on the base, a smooth affine relative curve maps finitely to A^1_S. After shrinking S, the branch divisor becomes finite étale over S. The preimage of its complement is then a finite étale cover of a type-(0,ν) fibration whose boundary is finite étale but not necessarily split, so ν counts geometric points. Shrinking X this way is harmless for neighbourhood bases. Care is needed with uniformity in the base and with keeping the K(π,1) and exactness properties of the fibration sequence, but no outright error appears.
'Curves of type (0,ν2) over K1' and 'relative curves over a curve over Q' are two descriptions of the same step (generic fibre versus model). The text runs them together loosely.

ideas.what: Build the Galois groupoids E_K for all fields K of finite type over Q inductively from E_Q, using that K is a finite extension of a purely transcendental extension.
ideas.modern_name: Transcendence-basis induction; iterated fundamental-group extensions (homotopy exact sequence)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. IX-XIII; La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Every point of a smooth variety over a field has a fundamental system of neighbourhoods that are iterated fibrations, where each step is a genus-0 curve fibration of type (0,ν) or a finite étale cover of such.
ideas.modern_name: Artin good neighbourhoods / elementary fibrations, refined to genus-0-up-to-étale-cover; compare hyperbolic polycurve neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Artin (SGA 4 XI) for elementary fibrations; Schmidt–Stix (2016) and Hoshi–Mochizuki for hyperbolic polycurve neighbourhood bases
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and the letter to Faltings mention neighbourhood bases by elementary anabelian varieties; the genus-0 refinement is not explicitly stated there as far as I know

ideas.what: Reconstruct smooth K-schemes, and their étale topoi, by gluing such elementary pieces described by profinite extensions and outer actions.
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian 'Lego' reconstruction; étale homotopy types of varieties
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3, letter to Faltings (1983)

missed.claim: A program to generate the arithmetic fundamental groupoids of all smooth varieties over finitely generated fields from the genus-0 tower (P^1 minus points) and finite étale covers. It rests on a genus-0-up-to-étale-cover refinement of Artin neighbourhoods. The refinement and the resulting inductive construction of E_K are left unproved and unpursued.
missed.quote: et tous les modèles élémentaires, où à chaque cran la fibration est soit une courbe de genre 0, soit un rev. étale fini d'une telle fibration particulière. Sauf erreur, ça fait assez pour avoir un syst. fondamental de voisinages de tt point d'une X lisse sur un K
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would reduce Galois actions on fundamental groups of arbitrary smooth varieties to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-controlled genus-0 tower plus finite étale covers. That links GT-theory to the anabelian neighbourhood results of Schmidt–Stix in a way not usually made explicit.

deep.surprise_reason: Artin neighbourhoods and the anabelian Lego idea are known and published by Grothendieck himself. The specific genus-0-up-to-finite-étale-cover refinement, and using it to build all E_K from E_Q, is a modest unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'soit des courbes elliptiques de type (0,ν2)' should read 'soit des courbes relatives de type (0,ν2)'.
'issus d'chaque cran' should read 'où à chaque cran'.
'soit un courbes de genre 0' should read 'soit une courbe de genre 0'.
The crossed-out word between E_K and E_Q is illegible; the sense is 'construire finalement tous les E_K sur E_Q'.
